Where things stand:

  • Branch: claude/release-readiness in treams-rs has 25 local commits. Nothing is pushed and no PR is open.
  • Local checks: everything passes on the integrated branch with Python 3.12:
    • just check, the Rust tests, and the full test suite (2369 passed, 14 skipped because matplotlib isn't installed);
    • the strict docs build, the wheel license-bundle check and cargo-deny;
    • just check-wheel, the release-guard self-test, actionlint on all workflows, and the secret scan over full history.
  • Dependencies:
    • Rust: complex-bessel 0.3 plus a lockfile refresh.
    • Python: advect up to <0.4, jax up to <0.12, newest dev tools, and uv 0.12.22.
    • GitHub Actions: pinned to advect's current SHAs.
  • Test matrix like advect's:
    • Python 3.12–3.15, NumPy 2.1–2.5, and framework lower-bound and latest lanes.
    • Rust 1.94 and stable, the 5-platform wheel build, docs, the secret scan, Codecov, and a CI Success gate.
  • Release process like advect's: TestPyPI first, then a manual approval step, then GitHub release, PyPI and versioned docs. There's also a new mkdocs site, and the "private" wording is gone.

Two limits you should know about:

  • Python 3.14/3.15 test coverage is narrower. The upstream treams package, which the tests compare against, doesn't support 3.14 or later. On those versions about 47 comparison test modules are skipped, and the summary says so; they're still a hard requirement on 3.12/3.13. The 3.15 wheels can't be smoke-tested with the [io] extra, because h5py has no 3.15 wheels yet. The same gap affects the [torch] extra.
  • Some things can't be run from here. The macOS, Windows and Linux arm64 wheel builds, the Codecov upload and the TestPyPI/PyPI publishing will only be exercised on GitHub.

Not necessarily. The defects were in treams-rs's old port of SciPy's code, which modified the algorithm ("scaled high-order arithmetic"). The spec agent also noted that SciPy returns NaN at those defect inputs rather than wrong numbers. Whether SciPy itself has a bug needs evidence. First a quick direct check on the two example points:
Compare SciPy lpmv with mpmath at the two defect points

No firm answer yet. A quick check showed SciPy doesn't return the wrong numbers our old code did: at both example points SciPy 1.16.3's scipy.special.lpmv returns NaN, while the true values are finite (about 2.1e242 and −4.4e-87). The silently wrong values came from treams-rs's own adaptation of SciPy's code, not from SciPy.

That still leaves open whether those NaNs are a real SciPy bug or a documented limitation, and whether SciPy is silently wrong anywhere else. A three-agent check is running to answer that:

  • Sweep: runs SciPy 1.16.3, 1.18.1 and the latest SciPy special-functions source (XSF) over all 131k reference points.
  • Root cause: traces why SciPy returns NaN there and how our old port turned it into wrong numbers, and searches SciPy's history and tests for a known issue or documented limit.
  • Verifier: re-checks the true values with an independent high-precision method and tries to refute the other two.

I'll come back with the verdict and, if it holds up, minimal reproducers for a SciPy issue.
